title: Scheduler next-start search is expensive with many long tasks
summary: When nothing is eligible, select_task() calls indigo_scheduler_next_eligible() for every task, which checks the whole duration at every 5-minute candidate: about 577 x duration points x tasks, up to ~21M point checks for 128 tasks of 24 h, on the handler queue every IDLE_CHECK_INTERVAL. Next: precompute per-task point validity and use a sliding window, and add the planned 128-task performance test (phase 3).

resolution.evidence: Task 20261112231644-ae3b-scheduler-phase-3b: per-task tables of the first failing grid point make the interval check one lookup and let the next-start search skip failing stretches (indigo_scheduler_points_*); equivalence test points_match_reference, timing tests next_start_search_cost (128 tasks of 24 h, 10 rounds in about 1 ms) and performance (plan of 128 tasks in about 16 ms), see verification.md.
